spesim package review (teaching + method-testing focus)

Source: REVIEW_spesim.md

Date: 2026-02-11
Package site: https://ajsmit.github.io/spesim/
Repo: https://github.com/ajsmit/spesim
Version reviewed: 0.3.3 (per NEWS/site)

This document is a full, end-to-end review of spesim as a teaching and method-testing package for spatially structured ecological communities.

Executive summary

spesim’s core strengths are (i) a coherent “simulate → sample → analyse” pipeline in irregular domains, (ii) excellent teaching ergonomics (init files, clear vignettes, stable API guidance), and (iii) good alignment with canonical community-ecology diagnostics.

The main weaknesses are typical of a deliberately lightweight simulator: some models are heuristic rather than mechanistic; the domain/units are synthetic by default; and several outputs can be misinterpreted as “process inference” unless users read the model card.

The 0.3.3 audit layer (nearest-neighbour diagnostics, filtering checks, sampling rejection/exclusion summaries) is a strong step toward turning spesim into a “tutor that audits the user’s conceptual model”.

1) What spesim does well

1.1 Coherent pipeline for teaching and method testing

  • The workflow is conceptually clean and matches how students think:
    1. generate a domain, 2) generate a heterogeneous community, 3) place quadrats (field-design analogues), 4) compute site × species and common summaries.
  • spesim_run() provides a teaching-friendly entry point while leaving lower- level knobs accessible.

1.2 Sampling designs in irregular polygons are a differentiator

  • Having random / tiled / systematic / transect / Voronoi schemes in one package, for irregular domains, is unusually practical.
  • 0.3.3’s placement_audit attachment is exactly what method-testing needs: it surfaces boundary rejection/exclusion that otherwise stays hidden.

1.3 Documentation has strong “instructor ergonomics”

  • The addition of Start here + the model card + validation vignettes improves discoverability and expectation-setting.
  • The public API / stability guide is unusually mature for an early version.

1.4 Outputs align with common ecological questions

  • Rank–abundance, occupancy–abundance, SAR, distance–decay, rarefaction are exactly the outputs most people want when learning how sampling interacts with spatial heterogeneity.
  • Human-readable report is pedagogically valuable: it encourages narrative interpretation rather than black-box plotting.

1.5 The “audit” layer is directionally excellent

  • spesim_audit() provides quick, approximate checks that answer: “Did I actually get clustering?”, “Is filtering visible?”, “How much did the boundary constrain my design?”
  • The report’s Conceptual audit section is the right integration point.

2) Where the weaknesses are

2.1 Some core models are heuristic vs mechanistic

This is a design choice (lightweight, teachable), but it implies: - Parameters do not generally map to biological rates/processes. - Spatial patterns may be “consistent with” a process without being generated by a canonical process model (depending on settings).

The model card helps, but users can still over-interpret if they skip it.

2.2 Domain units / CRS and interpretability

  • The default domain is synthetic and unitless (now documented).
  • Gradients are rescaled to familiar units (°C, m, mm), which is pedagogically helpful but can mislead users into thinking they are simulating real-world geography unless they supply a real CRS/extent.

2.3 Audit diagnostics are useful but still approximate

  • NN ratio vs CSR is a good lightweight diagnostic, but it is not a substitute for edge-corrected Ripley K or pair-correlation functions in irregular windows.
  • Filtering audit is based on quadrat mean environments and abundance; it can be confounded by small sample sizes, sparse species, or strong interactions.

2.4 Scalability / performance

  • Some steps (e.g., repeated intersections, report per-quadrat summaries) can become slow for very large N or high-resolution grids.
  • This is fine for teaching, but method-testing may push sizes upward.

3) What it gets wrong (or risks getting wrong)

3.1 Risk: “named process” ≠ realised regime

Even with the audit layer, the package still risks a common teaching failure: users select a named process (e.g., “Strauss”) and assume the realised pattern is inhibited, when parameters may produce weak effects in practice.

0.3.3 mitigates this, but a stronger regime-classification framework would help (see Recommendations).

3.2 The audit signals are not yet formalised as pass/fail thresholds

Right now, audits are descriptive (“CSR-like”, “weak signal”). In teaching, people often want a red/amber/green judgement aligned with the conceptual model.

3.3 Sampling “inclusion probabilities” are only partially represented

  • Boundary rejection/exclusion is reported (good).
  • But inclusion probability is scheme-dependent and can be subtle:
    • systematic: grid-centre filtering,
    • tiled: tiling candidates,
    • transect: safe-area shrinkage and intersection geometry,
    • voronoi: suitability criterion + seed density.

The current audits provide the raw ingredients, but not yet a unified statement like “effective sampling frame shrank by X%” or “edge-loss is severe”.

4) Recommendations (numbered for implementation tracking)

R1. Add a regime classification summary with explicit thresholds ✅ (implemented in v0.3.4-dev)

Add a small helper (or extend spesim_audit()) that converts the audit metrics into a teaching-friendly judgement: - Example: spesim_regime(res) → list with green/amber/red grades + reasons for spatial, filtering, and sampling constraints.

Implementation idea: - spatial: use NN ratio bands (e.g., <0.85 clustered, 0.85–1.15 CSR-ish, >1.15 inhibited) and require minimum n. - filtering: require rho > 0.2 and slope < 0 with minimum occupied sites. - sampling: boundary exclusion > 50% triggers amber/red.

R2. Add an edge-corrected option when spatstat is available ✅ (implemented in v0.3.5-dev)

Provide optional spatstat-based checks that can be turned on via an argument: - spesim_audit(res, diagnostics = c("nn", "spatstat")) - If spatstat is installed: - convert domain to owin (proper polygon window), - compute K/L and pcf summaries for selected species.

R3. Standardise and document the placement_audit schema ✅ (implemented in v0.3.6-dev)

Right now placement_audit is scheme-dependent (reasonable), but you’ll get better downstream tooling if you standardise keys.

Implemented changes: - placement functions now attach audits via a shared helper and a permissive validator. - audits always include: scheme, n_requested, n_returned. - schemes include additional standard keys where applicable (candidates, attempts, safe-area fraction, etc.).

R4. Add effective sampling frame reporting (area-based) ✅ (implemented in v0.3.7-dev)

For each sampling scheme, report an area-based summary that captures the boundary constraint.

Implemented changes: - Added estimate_sampling_frame() (conservative buffer-by-half-diagonal) and record: - safe_area_fraction (effective sampling frame) - buffer_dist (half-diagonal) - quadrat_size - Placement functions now include safe_area_fraction in placement_audit. - audit_sampling_scheme() now prints “effective sampling frame (area fraction)”.

This provides a single interpretable number: “your sampling frame shrank to 62% of the domain due to boundary exclusion.”

R5. Add a filtering sanity plot helper ✅ (implemented in v0.3.8-dev)

Create a small plotting utility that overlays expected vs realised filtering.

Implemented as plot_filtering_response(res): - per gradient species: abundance vs per-quadrat mean environment - dashed line at configured optimum (natural units) - shaded tolerance band (+/- tol)

Pairs naturally with audit_environmental_filtering().

R6. Extend audit to report per-species occupied-quadrat counts ✅ (implemented in v0.3.9-dev)

Filtering checks can be unstable when the species is rare.

Implemented changes: - audit_environmental_filtering() now reports occupancy_sites (number of quadrats with abundance > 0). - The qualitative label becomes too_sparse_to_assess when occupancy is low (default threshold currently 5). - print.spesim_audit() now prints occupancy_sites alongside n_sites.

R7. Make the report’s “Conceptual audit” reproducible and configurable ✅ (implemented in v0.3.10-dev)

  • Keep current defaults (lightweight).

Implemented changes: - generate_full_report(res, include_audit = TRUE, audit_top_n = 6). - When include_audit = TRUE, the report runs spesim_audit(res, diagnostics = "nn") to avoid optional heavy dependencies and to keep report generation deterministic. - The filtering lines in the report now include occupancy (occ=...) when available.

R8. Provide a single “method-testing bundle” function ✅ (implemented in v0.3.11-dev)

Added spesim_method_test(): - runs a simulation from P or an init_file - returns res and audit (via spesim_audit()) - optionally returns standard analysis tables and plots (rank–abundance, occupancy–abundance, SAR, distance–decay, rarefaction; plus spatial/quadrats; and filtering response when gradients exist)

This reduces the “glue code” instructors write repeatedly.

R9. Add at least one vignette explicitly about method testing ✅ (implemented in v0.3.12-dev)

Added vignette: “Method testing with spesim” (vignettes/spesim-method-testing.Rmd).

It demonstrates: - comparing sampling schemes under the same underlying truth, - comparing a distance-decay summary across designs, - using audits (including occupancy_sites guards) to avoid over-interpretation.

R10. Performance notes: document safe upper bounds for teaching ✅ (implemented in v0.3.13-dev)

Added vignette: “Performance notes” (vignettes/spesim-performance.Rmd).

Includes conservative rules of thumb for interactive use: - N_INDIVIDUALS (teaching vs method-testing ranges) - N_QUADRATS typical ranges - SAMPLING_RESOLUTION guidance - practical tips (when to turn off advanced analysis; when summaries become undefined)

R11. Thoroughly test ALL code snippets/blocks ✅ (implemented in v0.3.14-dev)

Implemented an automated check to ensure all vignette code chunks (including chunks marked eval=FALSE) are at least syntactically valid: - tests/testthat/test-snippets.R uses knitr::purl() + parse() for every vignette.

Note: R CMD check already executes package examples and vignettes that are not under \dontrun{} / eval=FALSE. This additional test catches broken code blocks that are shown to users but not executed during rendering.

R12. A thorough check and fix of all warnings ✅ (implemented in v0.3.14-dev)

Removed build warnings by: - Aligning vignette YAML titles with \VignetteIndexEntry{} (model-card and validation vignettes). - Setting highlight: null for all rmarkdown::html_vignette outputs to avoid pandoc highlight deprecation warnings during pkgdown/vignette rendering.

5) Other packages with overlapping functionality

No single package matches spesim’s exact combination (irregular domains + quadrat design suite + built-in classic panels + teaching report), but several cover major components.

Closest conceptual neighbour in R

  • mobsim: community simulation with SAD + spatial patterns + sampling and biodiversity responses. Likely the nearest “same idea” for many users.

Point processes / spatial diagnostics (R)

  • spatstat (geom/random/explore): gold-standard simulation + inference + diagnostics (K, L, pcf, edge correction, irregular windows).

Community ecology analyses (R)

  • vegan: diversity indices, dissimilarities, SAR (specaccum), rarefaction.
  • iNEXT / iNEXT.3D: rarefaction/extrapolation focused on inference.
  • betapart: beta diversity partitioning (turnover/nestedness).
  • adespatial: spatial multivariate methods and related diagnostics.

Landscape / gradient simulation (R)

  • NLMR + landscapetools: neutral landscapes / synthetic surfaces (then you add community simulation/sampling yourself).

Outside R (partial overlap)

  • Python scikit-bio: community dissimilarities and diversity tooling (not a spatial simulator).
  • More mechanistic ecological simulators exist (individual-based / metacommunity models), but they are typically far more complex than spesim’s teaching-first design.

Notes on provenance

This review is based on the package website (home, reference, key vignettes), NEWS (0.3.1–0.3.3), and the design intent stated in the model card.

Implementation checklist (where each recommendation likely lives)

This is a practical “where do I change what?” index. It’s intentionally approximate—use it to jump to the right files/functions quickly.

R1. Regime classification summary with explicit thresholds

  • Add: R/regime.R (new) or extend R/audit.R
  • Touch:
    • spesim_audit() (add regime= output block)
    • print.spesim_audit() (print green/amber/red summary)
  • Docs:
    • new help topic spesim_regime() (or section in ?spesim_audit)

R2. Edge-corrected option using spatstat when available

  • Add: R/audit_spatstat.R (new; keep behind requireNamespace())
  • Touch:
    • R/audit.R: new argument diagnostics = c("nn", "spatstat")
  • Vignette:
    • extend vignettes/spesim-validation.Rmd with “irregular window owin” path

R3. Standardise/document the placement_audit schema

  • Touch: all quadrat placers:
    • R/quadrats_random.R
    • R/quadrats_system.R
    • R/quadrats_tiled.R
    • R/quadrats_transect.R
    • R/quadrats_voronoi.R
  • Add: a small validator helper (e.g., .validate_placement_audit())
  • Docs:
    • add a short section to vignettes/spesim-quadrat-placement.Rmd

R4. Effective sampling frame reporting (area-based)

  • Add/Touch:
    • R/audit.R → audit_sampling_scheme() to compute area fractions
    • possibly a new helper in R/quadrats_utils.R:
      • compute eroded domain for a given quadrat diagonal (random)
      • compute safe-area fraction (transect)
  • Report:
    • R/report.R “Conceptual audit” section: include safe_area_fraction etc.

R5. Filtering sanity plot helper

  • Add: R/plot_filtering.R (new): e.g., plot_filtering_response(res, species = ...)
  • Depends on:
    • calculate_quadrat_environment() (R/matrices.R)
    • res$P$GRADIENT parsing
  • Vignette:
    • add to vignettes/spesim-env-gradients.Rmd or spesim-validation.Rmd

R6. Per-species occupied-quadrat counts in filtering audit

  • Touch: audit_environmental_filtering() in R/audit.R
    • compute occupancy_sites = sum(abund > 0)
    • include in output + qualitative flags (“too_sparse_to_assess”)
  • Report:
    • R/report.R: include occupancy in filtering summary lines

R7. Make report audit reproducible and configurable

  • Touch: generate_full_report() in R/report.R
    • add args include_audit = TRUE, audit_top_n = 6
    • ensure report calls are deterministic given SEED (you already reset seeds in R/run.R)

R8. Single “method-testing bundle” function

  • Add: R/method_test.R (new): spesim_method_test()
  • Wraps:
    • spesim_run()
    • spesim_audit()
    • optional plot helpers (existing + R5)
  • Docs:
    • short section in README + Start here vignette

R9. Vignette explicitly about method testing

  • Add: vignettes/spesim-method-testing.Rmd (new)
  • Uses:
    • fixed underlying truth + multiple sampling schemes
    • audit outputs to interpret when a comparison is “unfair” due to sampling-frame shrinkage
  • Pkgdown:
    • add to _pkgdown.yml articles list

R10. Performance notes / safe upper bounds

  • Add:
    • a short “Performance” section in vignettes/spesim-start-here.Rmd
    • or a standalone vignettes/spesim-performance.Rmd
  • Reference:
    • call out heavy steps: sf::st_intersection, gradient resolution, quadrat counts
